newsitem.title: UK: Elf strike buoys European gasoline price.
newsitem.headline: Elf strike buoys European gasoline price.

text.p: The six-day-old strike by Elf Aquitaine refinery workers offered another crutch on Tuesday for European gasoline prices, already supported by an open arbitrage to the U.S.
Gasoline has grabbed the spotlight at a normally quiet time of year as refiners cranked up production of heating oil heading into winter, traders and analysts said.
Unions and managers at Elf agreed on Tuesday to hold concrete negotiations over pay and working conditions to try to resolve the strike.
Talks will start on Thursday.

"One hundred thousand barrels per day of gasoline production capacity in Europe is being shut off by the strike...It sounds small but we are living in a world of tight markets," said Peter Bogin, associate director at Cambridge Energy Research Associates in Paris.

"The fact this is having an impact on the U.S. is a strong indicator of the market we're dealing with right now," he said. "It's a bit more severe than otherwise because refineries are focusing on gas oil production."
Some traders estimated as much as 750,000 tonnes, or 6.375 million barrels, were heading to the U.S. from Europe in November and early December because of the arbitrage and normal commitments.
"(The strike) is a bullish factor...and I think basically the Americans are still looking" for gasoline, said one European gasoline trader.
The strike has crippled a quarter of French refinery capacity at the three Elf plants.
The three refineries, which make up three-quarters of Elf's European refining network, have a combined capacity of 440,000 barrels per day (bpd).
Elf normally produces about 100,000 bpd of gasoline from its total capacity and feeds about 60,000 bpd into the French market, Bogin said.
French gasoline demand, which is running at about 350,000 bpd, is divided into 45 percent leaded and 55 percent unleaded material including 98 octane, Bogin said.

France is also a traditional gasoline exporter, selling 84,000 bpd in 1995, primarily to Germany, Italy, Spain, Switzerland, the former Soviet Union and Iran, according to the International Energy Agency.
European gasoline stocks as of end-October were 153 million barrels, down 3.74 million from September and up 2.97 million from a year ago, according to Euroilstock Foundation.
European refinery utilisation stood at 87.37 pct in October from 89.08 pct in September, with gasoline production at 3.172 million bpd.
Traders said Elf was a small buyer of superplus and leaded gasoline on Tuesday in the Northwest Europe market, which was speculated to have been because of the strike.
They detected no further buying on Tuesday but expectations that Elf may resurface in the physical market added to the bullish sentiment.
"It's not to be sneezed at if it goes on for 10 days," said Leo Drollas at the Centre for Global Energy Studies in London.
The roughly 4.4 million barrels lost over a 10-day period would be 50,000 bpd over a quarter of total production, or three pct of total French consumption of refined products, he calculated.
He said the impact may be felt more on the middle distillate market.
Analysts said they will have to wait and see if refineries crank up gasoline output to take advantage of the higher prices.
